open_items: Version limitation: this extraction describes only the saved preprint. The citation record identifies a later journal article with a different title and author order; its results were not used and may differ.

Participant-level creativity SDs, numerical SEs, confidence intervals, and standardized effects are absent. Error bars in Figures 2a/2b are undefined and unlabelled; no uncertainty is estimated from graph heights.

The exact follow-up sample size and per-arm counts are not printed. Only the general N=61 beneath Table 1 covers its novelty/usefulness follow-up rows; it is retained with an explicit caveat and is not transferred to follow-up flexibility or diversity.

The timing descriptions conflict: the abstract says after 30 days of experiment completion, while the body calls the follow-up one month later and labels it Day 30. The exact elapsed time from final AI exposure is unresolved; delay_days preserves the abstract statement.

AUT follow-up novelty: Table 2a prints Control 2.40 and GPT 2.56, while Table 1 prints Estimate -3.69, t -2.12, and P 0.038. Section 3.1 instead says the follow-up creativity differences were not significant. The contradictory printed statistics are retained.
AUT follow-up usefulness: Table 2a prints Control 5.62 and GPT 5.55, while Table 1 prints Estimate -6.26, t -1.52, and P 0.135. The discrepancy is unresolved and no value is repaired.

Task 2 creativity/novelty labels conflict between Section 2.3, Table 2b, Table 1, and Figure 2b. The extraction follows the reconciled novelty coding; this should not be treated as an unambiguous overall-creativity primary outcome.
Task 2 usefulness is tested in Table 1/Figure 2b, but its rating procedure is not separately described and its means are not numerically printed. Expert-rater coding is provisional.
Day 7 Task 2 usefulness has a significant printed test, contrary to the text’s assertion that all post-withdrawal p-values were insignificant.

Diversity pair selection, pair counts, SBERT checkpoint/training data, inferential test, and uncertainty basis are not reported. The collective AUT p-value bounds do not provide numerical SEs; dispersion statistics have no uncertainty.

The blanket boldface significance notes under Tables 2a, 2b, and 3 are inconsistent with specific tests and baseline statements. They are retained as reporting issues rather than assigned to every unbolded contrast.

Several projected-embedding dispersion values contradict the narrative claim that ChatGPT always reduces dispersion, particularly Task 2 SDs and eigenvalue sums, AUT Day 3 and Day 7, and Task 2 Day 6 ellipse area.
No primary outcome is identified in the paper; the preregistration is linked but not described. Participant country and the AI model release year are not stated.
The paper gives inconsistent counts of tasks across the introduction, methods, and limitations; these were not used to derive any sample count or estimate.
notes: Independent extractor B extraction from the complete saved PDF and its markdown conversion, including the appendix. Every PDF page was text-extracted with pymupdf; tables, figures, and appendix were inspected. There is one randomized sample, with two task types and repeated daily observations; days and tasks are not independent studies. Task 2 is open-ended product idea generation, despite the paper calling it convergent thinking; it is not a right-answer test. Inventory: AUT novelty, usefulness, and flexibility each have contrasts for Days 2-7 and Day 30; product-solution novelty, usefulness, content quality, public favor, and market success each have Days 2-7 contrasts. Each task also has separate SBERT similarity, string matching, projected-embedding SD, sum-of-eigenvalues, and ellipse-area contrasts at the corresponding post-baseline times. This gives 51 creativity/quality contrasts and 65 diversity contrasts. The screening form’s outcome cap is not applied; outcomes mentioned only in its notes are included, and distinct diversity measures remain separate. Printed Table 1 differences and t statistics are control minus GPT and are not reversed. Exact figure p-value labels are transcribed when available; rounded Table 1 P Values remain in each source quote and note. No p-value is replaced by a significance bound merely because the table rounds it to zero. No effect, SD, SE, count of pairs, or numeric value from a graph was computed. Source row quotes preserve all original decimal precision; numeric JSON tokens also preserve that precision. Study and laboratory arm analysis counts use the stated complete laboratory sample and common analysis N; per-day counts are not separately printed. Follow-up counts remain qualified as described per estimate. The three table footnotes print: Numbers in bold are not significant, while the rests are significant (p ≤ .001). These generic claims conflict with specific tests and are not used as outcome-level evidence. Source precision and spelling are preserved even where reporting is inconsistent. No other paper’s extraction or another extractor’s extraction file was used.
